What are the $x$-intercepts of the parabola shown above?

![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/question-capture/13955472/assets/d4c21d6ce09ff32004a28d18d223fef7858c377bccb0eb532cf2dda29a545f5e.png)

The value of the $x$-intercept of the parabola shown above is{{field-1}}.
feedback.worked_solution:
First, we need to find the equation of the parabola. From the diagram, we see that the parabola has a vertex at $(-7,-2)$ and passes through the point $(-11,-6).$

The general standard equation of a left- or right-opening parabola with vertex $(h,k)$ is given by

$$
(y-k)^{2}=4p(x-h).
$$

Substituting $(h,k)=(-7,-2)$ into the above gives

$$
(y+2)^{2}=4p(x+7).
$$

Now, we need to find $p.$ Since the parabola passes through the point $(-11,-6),$ we substitute $x=-11$ and $y=-6$ into the equation and get

$$
\begin{aligned}(-6+2)^{2} & =4p(-11+7) \\ (-4)^{2} & =4p\cdot (-4) \\ 16 & =-16p \\ p & =-1.\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, the equation of the parabola is

$$
\begin{aligned}(y+2)^{2} & =-4(x+7).\end{aligned}
$$

When the parabola intersects the $x$-axis, we must have $y=0.$ So, we substitute $y=0$ into the equation of the parabola and solve for $x:$

$$
\begin{aligned}(0+2)^{2} & =-4(x+7) \\ 4 & =-4(x+7) \\ -1 & =x+7 \\ x & =-8\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, the $x$-intercept is $-8.$
